chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Sama'ah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who acquired wealth from the work of the Umayyads, and he gives charity from it, maintains kinship ties from it, and performs Hajj so that Allah may forgive what he earned, while he says, 'Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, one sin does not expiate another sin, but a good deed removes a sin.' Then he said, 'If he mixed the forbidden with the permissible, so they became mixed together and he cannot distinguish the permissible from the forbidden, then there is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on spending wealth from the Umayyads in charity and Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the expiation of sins through good deeds and the specific ruling on mixed wealth from the Umayyads, noting that while charity and Hajj remove sins, they do not cancel one sin with another. He further clarifies that if the haram and halal portions are thoroughly mixed and indistinguishable, there is no harm in using the entire amount for worship and charity. This ruling reflects the Shia principle of ease in cases of uncertainty regarding the purity of wealth acquired during periods of political transition.
